title: fix(devx): hold the cross-package gate's bare-specifier boundary to its own premise
body:
Fixes #18236

Clause-②: no

`File surface:` — one path, `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`. No `turbo.json`, no
`.changeset/*.md`, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed surface. Why each of those stayed shut is
measured below, not asserted.

## The card's premise, re-taken on `origin/main` — and one half of it is falsified

The card's mechanism is: `packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts` consumes
`ListViewSchema.sort` through the **bare** specifier `@objectstack/spec`, that specifier is excluded
by the gate's import-side boundary, therefore the coupling is invisible to **both** the
affected-subset filter and the turbo cache. The first two links hold — the import is bare (`:37`)
and the gate does skip it. The third does not, and it is the one the fix would have rested on.

Measured on `62d830e54e`, turbo 2.10.10, with a firing control beside each reading:

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| `turbo ls --affected` for a diff touching ONLY `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` | **76 of 81** packages, `@objectstack/cli` among them |
| the same document after the real `--union-into` | 76, unchanged (`No cross-package scan declares inputs touched by this diff.`) |
| `@objectstack/cli#test` turbo hash, view.zod.ts pristine | `09d6dde83abb1ddf` |
| the same hash, view.zod.ts mutated (marker count 0 to 1 on disk) | `2d8ebbbb4202c0e5` — **moves** |
| CONTROL: the same hash, an unrelated package mutated instead (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-params-contract.dogfood.test.ts`, marker count 0 to 1) | `09d6dde83abb1ddf` — unmoved, so the instrument is specific |
| **PM 补的 Layer A 亮控**(复核时第一手加测):同一条 `turbo ls --affected` 钉 `TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD` 后,**干净树读 0 packages**;只改 `view.zod.ts` 读 76,含 `@objectstack/cli` | ⚠️ **不钉 base 时干净树也读 76** —— 上面第一行那个 76 单独看不区分「改了」和「没改」;钉了 base 之后结论不变 |

⇒ **the PROBE the card asks for already passes, before any change.** Layer A reaches
`@objectstack/cli` through the dependency graph, and Layer B moves because `@objectstack/cli#test`
dependsOn its own `build`, which dependsOn `^build`, which folds `@objectstack/spec#build`'s hash in.
`packages/cli/package.json` has declared `"@objectstack/spec": "workspace:*"` throughout, including
at `1e20f816e^` (checked on that tree, not recalled).

## Why that answers all three of the seat's questions at once, with numbers

Measured over all 3714 test sources under `packages/`, `apps/` and `examples/`:

| | |
|---|--:|
| test files importing a workspace sibling by BARE specifier | 2010 |
| bare workspace specifier occurrences | 3692 |
| distinct (importer, imported) package pairs | 349 |
| distinct importing packages / imported packages | 66 / 55 |
| **pairs NOT backed by an edge on the importer's manifest** | **0** |

1. **How should bare specifiers be admitted?** They should not. A bare specifier resolves only
   because the importing package declares the target — that is what pnpm's strict linking means —
   and that declaration is an edge on the graph both CI layers already walk. All 349 pairs have one.
2. **Can turbo express it?** It does not have to. The coupling is already in turbo's own dependency
   graph, so `turbo.json` needs no new `inputs` entry and this diff touches none.
3. **Does the fix put every package's suite on every sibling?** The card's route 2 would: the
   natural glob is `packages/TARGET/src/**`, so 349 declarations across 66 packages pointing at 55
   siblings' whole source trees — the explosion the boundary was written to prevent — for **zero**
   coverage, since the graph carries every pair. Refused on that measurement. The affected subset
   after this PR is byte-for-byte the subset before it: **0 declarations added, 0 packages moved.**

## What IS wrong, and what this PR changes

The boundary asserts a conclusion ("a bare specifier is an installed dependency, never a repo source
input") while nothing checks its premise. That premise fails the moment a bare specifier names a
workspace package the importer does **not** declare, and such an import still resolves whenever
something else supplies it — a vitest `resolve.alias`, a hoisted `node_modules`, a tsconfig path.
Then there is no manifest edge, no graph edge, no glob and **no flag**: #7802 by a sixth spelling,
arriving through the one door this file had declared safe on reasoning rather than on a check.

So the exclusion stays and becomes conditional, with the condition enforced every run:

> A bare specifier is excluded from the radius roster BECAUSE it is an installed dependency. Every
> bare specifier naming a workspace package must therefore be declared as one by the package
> importing it.

`bareWorkspaceImportCensus()` is its own walk, not a second output of `findEscapingPackages()`: that
walk opens with a `FS_READ`-or-ascending-literal pre-filter which a file importing only bare
specifiers never passes — precisely the file this question is about. The verdict line now prints the
live census, so the limb's steady-state silence is a measurement rather than an absence:

```
OK: 29 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared, and turbo.json hashes every declared glob
(6 of them on a split "test:repo" task); 13 walked root(s) judged, 3 on ACCEPTED_WALK_RADII;
2010 test file(s) import a workspace sibling by bare specifier over 349 package pair(s), every one declared.
```

Those two numbers are produced by the gate and agree with the independent scan above, which was
written first and separately.

## Red before green — named gate, shown red, on the incident file itself

The gate that can go red here is `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs`, and the ablation deletes
the one manifest edge the premise rests on. Committed first, then mutated, then restored.

| leg | on-disk proof | `check:cross-package-test-inputs` |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | — | **exit 0**, the OK line above |
| mutated: `"@objectstack/spec": "workspace:*"` deleted from `packages/cli/package.json` | deleted-text count **1 to 0**; `git diff HEAD --name-only` 0 to 1 line; the mutated manifest still parses as JSON | **exit 1**, 92 findings |
| restored | `git hash-object` equals the `HEAD` blob (`5d84eb3ea…`); `git diff HEAD --name-only` back to **0** lines | — |

The decisive finding under mutation names the incident file and the incident import:

```
- @objectstack/cli imports the workspace package `@objectstack/spec` from a test and does not declare it.
      packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts
        @objectstack/spec
```

No rebuild leg is owed and none is claimed: this gate is a `scripts/*.mjs` source scan invoked
directly by node, with no `dist/` anywhere in its resolution path, so the mutation reached the code
under test the moment it reached disk.

Direction declared before the run and observed: **turns red** — the ordinary direction.

## Controls

- ⭐ **LIT CONTROL.** The incident file's two relative imports (`:38` `../src/utils/format`, `:39`
  `./helpers/serve-process.js`) were already visible to the roster half and still are: this diff
  touches no code on that path, and `check:cross-package-test-inputs` reports the same 29 escaping
  packages, the same 13 walked roots and the same 3 accepted radii before and after.
- ⭐ **DARK CONTROL, two halves.** `vitest`, `zod` and `node:fs` must read 0 — pinned by new
  self-test cases one per shape, beside the three pre-existing `does NOT flag` cases that the
  #10452 boundary already carried. And the affected subset must not balloon: it does not move by a
  single package, because this limb adds no declaration and no glob (0 of 349 pairs are findings).
- ⭐ **PROBE.** Satisfied before and after, by the graph rather than by this gate — the measurement
  at the top of this body is the evidence, taken with its own firing control.

## Gates

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| 30 commands derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` | see the run table in the report; all exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs --self-test` | **214** cases (was 191), exit 0, verdict line reached |
| `node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff …` | **NOT MEASURED** — exit 0 while judging nothing: `scripts/**` is covered by no declared surface, so no tell could have fired whatever the diff contains |
| `node scripts/check-published-list-mirrors.mjs` | exit 0 — `RECOGNISED_PATH_SPELLINGS` is untouched; only `RECOGNISED_IMPORT_SPELLINGS`, which no mirror row declares, gains four comment lines |
| control characters | `grep -naP` over the changed file: 0 hits, beside `pnpm check:nul-bytes` |

`skip-changeset`: nothing here publishes. `scripts/` sits at the repo root, outside every package
directory, so no package's `files[]` can ship it; the only packages that name this script do so in
turbo `inputs`, which is hashing, not shipping.

## Acceptance notes

- **The incident's actual cause is still open, and it is not this gate.** CI evidence from #17914's
  own run (34746808828, `Test Core`): the timing table reports
  `cache-replayed packages, excluded as non-measurements: 1 (@objectstack/cli)` and marks every
  `@objectstack/cli` row `replayed log` — so `@objectstack/cli#test` was a turbo cache REPLAY on the
  PR that reddened `main`, and the suite never ran. That contradicts the hash measurement above,
  which shows the task hash moving for exactly that diff. One of the two readings is about a
  mechanism nobody has named yet. Reported to the dispatching seat as a finding to file; it is the
  link that actually let #17914 through, and it survives this PR untouched.
- The `queue-flake anchor` naming convention (#18032) is noted, not filed here: it is a triage
  narrative question, and it already carries its own "This issue is a NAME, not a diagnosis" line.
